newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND CAN ONLY WATCH, WAIT FOR OVERALL TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND CAN ONLY WATCH, WAIT FOR OVERALL TITLE.

text.p: The racing is over for Luc Alphand, but the tension will continue to build for the French speed specialist during the last two days of competition at the World Cup Finals.

Alphand sits atop the overall standings poised for an historic World Cup championship. His fate, however, will be determined by the results of Norwegian Kjetil Andre Aamodt in Saturday's giant slalom and the season-ending slalom on Sunday.
"I will be an active spectator," said the 31-year-old Alphand, who joked that he might use Friday's off-day to find pins and a voodoo doll to combat Aamodt in the technical events.
Said Aamodt: "He has done a good job this year. Now he just has to sit back and watch. It's me who has the hard work now."
The only other title at stake in the four remaining races this weekend is in men's slalom, where leader Thomas Sykora and fellow-Austrian Thomas Stangassinger will duel.
The main drama of the weekend, however, centres on the men's overall title.

Hoping to become the first Frenchman to win the overall title since the great Jean-Claude Killy 29 years ago, Alphand leads Aamodt by 106 points after surrendering points in the speed races, which he had dominated this year.

Momentum may be in the corner of the 1994 World Cup champion from Norway, who improved his chances by whittling away at the deficit in Thursday's Super-G. Alphand won the season title but finished ninth to Aamodt's fifth Friday.
Alphand, winner of three successive downhill titles, blamed his ninth-place finish in Wednesday's downhill on his skis, then griped that windy conditions hurt him in the Super-G.
Later, the Frenchman admitted he was just plain worn out.
"I am too mentally tired," said Alphand, who has broadly hinted that this would be his last season. "I'm on empty."

Alphand would become the first speed specialist ever to claim the overall crown. Italian star Alberto Tomba, who will make his first appearance in the Finals this weekend, won the 1995 overall title racing only technical events -- winning 11 times in slalom and giant slaloms.
Alphand insists that he is completely satisfied with his season, come what may.
"It has been a great season. Finishing second in the overall championship would not be a failure," he said.

As drained as Alphand feels, the Frenchman knows what his rival has gone through to try and catch him. In the last three weeks the Norwegian all-rounder has travelled from Norway to Japan to the United States in his relentless pursuit of the coveted overall crown.
Aamodt has already achieved one momentous comeback in Vail.

Three years ago, he was 13th after the first run of the giant slalom at the World Cup Finals here before making a brilliant second run for a victory that helped him win the overall crown from the great Marc Girardelli.
"I admire Aamodt for what he has done," said Alphand. "I would not be ashamed to lose to Aamodt."
